Subject: Draft MAP & outcome rubric for Medsync evaluation

Hannah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our discussion I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that ties evaluation activities to concrete acceptance criteria and a proposed close runway. High level:

- Two-week evaluation window (4 total business weeks if counting onboarding + run).
- Acceptance criteria split across Safety/Privacy, Latency/Throughput, and Concordance (domain accuracy).
- Exit gates are explicit: onboarding complete -> smoke pass -> signed acceptance tests -> procurement signoff.

Please see the attached "Medsync_MAP_v2.xlsx" for the live checklist. A few asks for you:
1) Confirm target pilot cohort (sample size / query mix).
2) Flag any compliance/feature must-haves (PII redaction, logging retention).
3) Desired close date if evaluation is successful.

If that works, we can lock the timeline and I’ll loop in Marissa on commercial steps and Aditya on any technical integration tasks.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@medsync.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & outcome rubric for Medsync evaluation

Hannah — thanks, great questions. Short answers first: yes, 1500 encounters is a workable sample for initial concordance; we typically recommend stratifying by case complexity (low/med/high) and ensuring at least 200 high-complexity cases.

On retention & access: Redwood Private preserves logs and VM-level artifacts per the MAP; we can configure a 30-day retention window and provide a read-only audit bundle for your compliance team. Aditya — can you confirm the retention config and whether a SOC2-friendly bundle is straightforward?

Suggested acceptance thresholds (proposed):
- Concordance (clinical labeling/agreement): >= 92% overall, with no sub-cohort below 88%.
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 350ms for short prompts, P95 <= 800ms for long sequences used by your use-case.
- Reliability: <1% error rate (5xx/timeout) during test window.

Example acceptance test (excerpt):
- Test: Medication reconciliation prompt set (n=250)
  - Passing condition: system output matches clinician adjudicated label >= 93%
  - Measurement: blind evaluation by two clinicians, tie-breaker by third.

Attached is "Medsync_acceptance_examples.pdf" with three exemplar tests and expected reporting format.

Proposed close runway:
- Week 0: Onboarding & dataset transfer (3 business days)
- Week 1: Integration smoke & baseline inference runs
- Week 2: Primary acceptance tests (concordance + perf)
- Week 3: Wrap, review results, executive signoff + procurement kickoff

If you confirm the cohort and retention, we will:
- Lock the acceptance tests and schedule the runs
- Marissa will prepare the commercial proposal tied to the MAP milestones
- I’ll book a short review session for Week 3 to go through the pass/fail report

Best,
Ben
[Attachment: Medsync_acceptance_examples.pdf (pdf)]
